absent: Runtime set and get callback invocation context, error propagation and permission enforcement beyond descriptor fields.
Real locking protocol for concurrent parameter access when the no-op shims are replaced.
Sysfs entry lifetime, visibility rules and removal ordering for parameters.
PMU interrupt handling flow, overflow behavior and event scheduling beyond callback signatures.
Validation and meaning of filter settings, format field positions and capability bitmap contents.
Boot argument parsing order across levels and interaction with the unknown-argument handler.

findings.text: A parameter declaration produces a resident descriptor in a dedicated parameter section carrying a flattened name string, owning module reference, operations table pointer, validated permission bits, numeric level and flags word plus a generic argument slot, with build-time checks that the name prefix fits the module name limit and that the descriptor keeps natural alignment for its type.

Callback parameters share one registration path distinguished only by level and flags: the generic module form uses level minus one with no flags while the unsafe variant adds the unsafe flag, and built-in stages map core, postcore, arch, subsys, fs, device and late to levels one through seven respectively with empty flags.

Typed helpers first run a compile-time storage check for the named variable and then register it with the type-specific operations table, using the module name prefix for module forms and an empty prefix for core forms; unsafe core and named-unsafe module variants set the unsafe flag, and one call form builds a local operations table from caller-supplied set and get handlers with cleared flags before registration.

Each scalar checker expands through a common helper that declares an unused function returning a pointer to the expected storage type, so mismatched variable types fail at build time; byte, short, ushort, int, uint, long, ulong, ullong, char pointer and boolean families each bind to their natural C type, with hex integer sharing unsigned integer handling, bint sharing integer handling and enable-only boolean sharing boolean handling, while inverted boolean still expects boolean storage.

String parameters keep a small read-only descriptor holding a length bound and a pointer to the caller buffer and are serviced by dedicated string operations, while array parameters keep a read-only descriptor holding a capacity derived from the C array size, a pointer to a live element count, a pointer to the element operations table, an element byte size and a base pointer, serviced by shared array operations; a shorthand aliases the parameter name to the array name and records a human-readable array-of-type tag.

Hardware-related parameters behave like ordinary typed or array parameters except that they set a hardware marker flag in the registration flags word, and a separate enumeration classifies the intended hardware resource as port, memory address, either port or memory, interrupt line, DMA channel, DMA buffer address or other value without affecting the storage check.

In the routed configuration the parameter serialization helpers for a module accept a module pointer and perform no action, so callers cannot rely on them for exclusion and must treat any real locking as provided elsewhere if at all.

Module sysfs setup reports success without work and removal does nothing, ACPI PMU probing reports success without work, and host PMU initialization for virtualization expands to an empty statement, meaning all four are disabled-configuration shims rather than functional entry points in these fragments.

Unknown boot or module argument handling is delegated to a callback receiving the parameter text, an optional value text, a doing-what context string and an opaque argument with an integer status result, while ARM PMU driver binding is delegated to an initializer receiving the PMU container and returning an integer status.

Per-CPU PMU hardware state holds a fixed table of active event pointers indexed by counter, a bitmap marking which counters are in use, a back pointer to the owning PMU for per-CPU interrupt context, an interrupt number, a branch-stack record pointer and a count of active events requesting branch records.

The ARM PMU container embeds a generic PMU core plus a supported-CPU mask, a driver name, handlers for interrupts, per-event enable and disable, counter index allocation and release, event filtering, counter read and write, and whole-unit start, stop and reset, plus event mapping helpers including a virtualization mapping hook, a counter mask, a 32-bit-only secure-access flag, a platform device link, per-CPU hardware state, a global list node, a CPU power-management notifier, a null-terminated attribute-group table, version and cycle-counter avoidance controls, identification registers, two common-event capability bitmaps and an ACPI CPU identifier.

Attribute groups appear in the fixed order common, events, formats and capabilities followed by a count sentinel, and the container reserves one extra slot beyond the count so the table can be null terminated.

PMU model probing uses a table entry carrying a CPU identifier, a mask selecting significant identifier bits and an initializer callback, with constructor helpers for plain CPU-part matching and for Intel XScale version matching using a composite mask over implementer, variant and architecture fields.

Maximum simultaneous hardware events is 32 in one configuration and 33 in the alternate configuration; event width capabilities use bit 0 for 64-bit, bit 1 for 47-bit and bit 2 for 63-bit; unmappable hardware and cache operations both use sentinel 65535, with helpers that prefill the full hardware map and the full cache type-operation-result cube with that sentinel.

ARMv8 PMU topology facts are 31 general counters, cycle counter index 31, instruction counter index 32 with a note that the latter is not reachable from 32-bit mode, 64 common events and extended common base 16384; platform device names are armv8-pmu for the core PMU, arm,spe-v1 for statistical profiling and arm,trbe for trace buffering.

Common architectural event codes occupy 0x0000 through 0x003F inclusive in a dense assignment starting with software increment and covering first-level instruction and data cache and TLB behavior, retired loads stores instructions and branches, exceptions and returns, context and program-counter writes, mispredictions, cycles, memory and bus activity, second and third level cache hierarchy and TLBs, last-level and remote behavior, table walks, speculative versus retired operations and frontend and backend stall attribution.

Extended codes use 0x4000 to 0x4003 for sampling-engine stages, 0x4004 to 0x4005 for activity-monitor cycles and backend memory stall, 0x4006 and 0x4009 to 0x400B for long-miss cache behaviors, 0x400C and 0x400E for trace-buffer wrap and trigger, 0x4010 to 0x4013 and 0x4018 to 0x401B for trace and cross-trigger outputs, 0x4020 to 0x4022 for alignment latency, and 0x4024 to 0x4026 for checked memory accesses.

Format helpers render a configuration field as a name plus bit or bit-range suffix for sysfs, and extraction helpers recover a named field by shifting the chosen configuration word and masking to the field width, with single-bit fields using a bare index and wider fields using a low-high range.

The parameter descriptor qualifier has two build configurations, one expanding to empty for writable descriptors and one expanding to read-only, allowing the same registration macro to serve both mutable and immutable parameter tables.

Unsafe registration marks parameters whose runtime update or callback execution needs extra caution, string and array descriptors alias caller-owned buffers and counters so lifetime and concurrent mutation matter, and hardware-marked values feed hardware configuration where invalid input can affect device behavior.

Counter use follows allocation of an index from the free set, optional filtering, per-event enable, whole-unit start, counter reads and writes during activity, per-event disable, whole-unit stop and release of the index, with a separate reset operation restoring unit state.
Both perf headers use include guards that define a unique macro on first inclusion so repeated inclusion has no effect.
